expectations.text: Rejects the built-in `errors` array as the only failure channel for a third-party surface.
expectations.evidence: "No, extensions.code alone isn't enough... leaves three of your five failures in the wrong channel."

expectations.text: Recommends the hybrid split as the default posture rather than one single mechanism for everything.
expectations.evidence: Table splits result type vs top-level errors.

expectations.text: Assigns the server fault (Postgres statement timeout), malformed queries, and the authentication failure (expired token) to the built-in top-level `errors`.
expectations.evidence: "Expired token and DB timeout do belong in top-level errors."

expectations.text: Assigns the expected business outcomes (card declined, region ineligibility, duplicate refund) to union or interface result types expressed in the schema.
expectations.evidence: Card declined, region, refund already issued -> result type.

expectations.text: Writes at least one concrete result union naming its success member and its distinct business-failure members.
expectations.evidence: "union SubscriptionCreateResult = | SubscriptionCreateSuccess | PaymentDeclined | PlanNotAvailableInRegion | ValidationError"

expectations.text: States that a union result makes every possible outcome visible in the schema, so a client cannot silently skip a failure mode the way it can with an untyped error body.
expectations.evidence: "nothing in the schema tells an integrator that subscriptionCreate can decline, so they can't discover it from introspection or codegen"

expectations.text: Keeps a shared `ErrorCode` enum under the chosen posture so clients switch on stable codes while message text stays free to change.
expectations.evidence: "enum ErrorCode {...}" and "message: free text, may change, never a contract"

expectations.text: Identifies the regex-on-message-text breakage as the symptom of having no stable machine-readable code, not as the integrator's mistake.
expectations.evidence: Says codes fix the regex problem and integrator should migrate; does not frame it as not their mistake.

expectations.text: Declines to promote result types onto every query as well, and names routine partial data from flaky-upstream-backed fields as the condition that would promote it.
expectations.evidence: Queries are never discussed.

expectations.text: Notes that adding a union to an already-shipped field is a breaking change, so a schema several teams will extend for years should adopt result types early.
